items.groupHeader: Questions 1 to 4 are based on the conversation you have just heard.
items.stemEn: What does the woman say about the food at the canteen?

options.textEn: It is absurdly expensive.
It is appropriately priced.
It brings shame on the university.
It caters to students and teachers.

options.text: 价格高得离谱。
定价合理。
给大学带来了耻辱。
能满足师生的需求。

review.questionTranslation: 女士说食堂的食物怎么样？

evidence.location: 解析册·听力原文 [1] 下划线标注（listening.long_conversations.1）
evidence.quote: I don't actually. I personally think they're perfectly appropriate.

review.explanation: 对话开头，男士表示食堂的食物价格高得离谱，女士随即表示她并不赞同这一观点，她个人觉得价格非常合理。由此可知，B项为正确答案，同时排除A项。C项是对对话内容的错误理解，故排除。虽然对话中女士说她觉得食物挺好的，但她并没有扩大到师生的层面，故排除D项。
distractors: 同时排除A项。C项是对对话内容的错误理解，故排除。虽然对话中女士说她觉得食物挺好的，但她并没有扩大到师生的层面，故排除D项。

items.groupHeader: Questions 1 to 4 are based on the conversation you have just heard.
items.stemEn: How does the woman feel about the canteen's sweet things or fancy delicacies?

options.textEn: They never really appeal to her.
They are never actually good value.
They are within students' budgets.
They always come at a high speed.

options.text: 它们从来都没有真正吸引她。
它们实际上从来都不划算。
它们在学生预算范围内。
它们总是很快上桌。

review.questionTranslation: 女士对食堂的甜食或精致点心感觉如何？

evidence.location: 解析册·听力原文 [2] 下划线标注（listening.long_conversations.1）
evidence.quote: I never really crave sweet things or any fancy delicacies.

review.explanation: 对话中间，两人开始讨论食堂甜点的价格，两人都认为甜点贵了，并且女士说：“我从来不喜欢甜食或精致的点心。”因此A项为正确答案，同时排除C项。对话中女士并未评价甜点是否物有所值，故排除B项。D项在对话中虽有提及，但这是对炒蛋的描述，而不是甜点，故排除。
distractors: 同时排除C项。对话中女士并未评价甜点是否物有所值，故排除B项。D项在对话中虽有提及，但这是对炒蛋的描述，而不是甜点，故排除。

items.groupHeader: Questions 1 to 4 are based on the conversation you have just heard.
items.stemEn: What does the man say is one of the best things about the canteen?

options.textEn: The food.
The space.
The speed.
The environment.

options.text: 食物。
空间。
速度。
环境。

review.questionTranslation: 男士说食堂最好的一点是什么？

evidence.location: 解析册·听力原文 [3] 下划线标注（listening.long_conversations.1）
evidence.quote: Actually, that's one of the best things about the canteen, the speed.

review.explanation: 对话中，两人说到食堂的好处时，男士明确表示：“其实，这是食堂最好的地方之一，就是速度快。”由此可知，C项为正确答案。

items.groupHeader: Questions 1 to 4 are based on the conversation you have just heard.
items.stemEn: What did the canteen undergo a few years ago?

options.textEn: A complete refurnishing.
A ruinous burning down.
A substantial expansion.
A massive renovation.

options.text: 装备全部更新。
毁灭性的烧毁。
大幅扩建。
大规模翻新。

review.questionTranslation: 食堂几年前经历了什么？

evidence.location: 解析册·听力原文 [4] 下划线标注（listening.long_conversations.1）
evidence.quote: Apparently, they did a massive renovation a few years ago.

review.explanation: 对话最后，女士说道：“显然，几年前他们进行了一次大规模翻新。”D项为原文原词，故正确。其他三项在对话中均未提及，故排除。
distractors: 其他三项在对话中均未提及，故排除。

items.groupHeader: Questions 5 to 8 are based on the conversation you have just heard.
items.stemEn: According to the woman, what view about today's young people is not really justified?

options.textEn: They have a poor work ethic.
They don't get along with managers.
They are struggling in the workplace.
They aren't as varied as their predecessors.

options.text: 他们职业道德差。
他们与经理相处得不好。
他们在职场中挣扎。
他们不如上一代人多元。

review.questionTranslation: 根据女士的说法，对于现在的年轻人，哪种观点其实并不合理？

evidence.location: 解析册·听力原文 [5] 下划线标注（listening.long_conversations.2）
evidence.quote: We often hear young people today have a poor work ethic.

review.explanation: 对话开头，女士提到：“我们常听说现在的年轻人职业道德差，但这种说法并不合理，对吧？”男士回答：“确实不合理。”由此可知，A项为正确答案。B、C两项对话中未提及，故排除。对话中，男士说道：“实际上，这个年龄段的年轻人和其他任何一代人一样，都是多元且多面的。”D项与此不符，而且这也不是女士的说法，故排除。
distractors: B、C两项对话中未提及，故排除。对话中，男士说道：“实际上，这个年龄段的年轻人和其他任何一代人一样，都是多元且多面的。”D项与此不符，而且这也不是女士的说法，故排除。

items.groupHeader: Questions 5 to 8 are based on the conversation you have just heard.
items.stemEn: What does the man say is important for managers to get along better with young workers?

options.textEn: Learning about the way they adhere to their own values.
Recognizing how they try to strike a work-life balance.
Knowing how they struggle to connect with managers.
Understanding the way they seek career advancement.

options.text: 了解他们如何坚持自己的价值观。
认识到他们如何努力平衡工作与生活。
知道他们如何努力与经理建立联系。
理解他们追求职业发展的方式。

review.questionTranslation: 男士说管理者要更好地与年轻员工相处，重要的是什么？

evidence.location: 解析册·听力原文 [6] 下划线标注（listening.long_conversations.2）
evidence.quote: It's also really important to recognize the way young people want to balance their work life with their personal life.

review.explanation: 对话中，男士说道：“同样重要的是认识到年轻人想要平衡工作与个人生活的方式。”由此可知，B项为正确答案。对话中，虽然男士提到要了解年轻人的价值观，但没有表示要了解他们如何坚持自己的价值观，故排除A项。C、D两项在对话中并未提及，故排除。
distractors: 对话中，虽然男士提到要了解年轻人的价值观，但没有表示要了解他们如何坚持自己的价值观，故排除A项。C、D两项在对话中并未提及，故排除。

items.groupHeader: Questions 5 to 8 are based on the conversation you have just heard.
items.stemEn: How do young people measure their productivity levels according to the man?

options.textEn: In terms of the number of hours spent.
By the amount of work they perform.
In terms of the work done in 8 hours.
By the quality of the work they do.

options.text: 从所花费的时长来看。
按他们完成的工作量。
从8小时内完成的工作来看。
依据他们的工作质量。

review.questionTranslation: 根据男士的说法，年轻人如何衡量自己的工作效率水平？

evidence.location: 解析册·听力原文 [7] 下划线标注（listening.long_conversations.2）
evidence.quote: Instead, young people measure their productivity levels by the quality of the work they perform.

review.explanation: 对话中，男士说道：“相反，年轻人通过工作质量来衡量自己的工作效率水平。”由此可知，D项为正确答案。在说到年轻人的工作效率时，男士表示年轻人认为工作效率不应以工作时长来衡量，故排除A项。B项在原文中并未提及，故排除。对话中男士以“8小时工作”为例是为了说明时间长不等于工作效率高，故排除C项。
distractors: 在说到年轻人的工作效率时，男士表示年轻人认为工作效率不应以工作时长来衡量，故排除A项。B项在原文中并未提及，故排除。对话中男士以“8小时工作”为例是为了说明时间长不等于工作效率高，故排除C项。

items.groupHeader: Questions 5 to 8 are based on the conversation you have just heard.
items.stemEn: What companies does the man think would appeal to young workers?

options.textEn: Those whose culture facilitates their advancement.
Those allowing them to do projects of their choice.
Those whose values align with their own.
Those refraining from discrediting their perspectives.

options.text: 那些企业文化促进他们晋升的公司。
那些允许他们做自选项目的公司。
那些价值观与他们一致的公司。
那些不贬低他们观点的公司。

review.questionTranslation: 男士认为什么样的公司会吸引年轻员工？

evidence.location: 解析册·听力原文 [8] 下划线标注（listening.long_conversations.2）
evidence.quote: They must feel the need to stay working at a company whose values align with their own.

review.explanation: 对话最后，男士明确说道：“他们必须感受到有必要留在与自己的价值观一致的公司工作。”由此可知，C项为正确答案。其他三项中的文化、自选项目和贬低观点对话中男士均未提及，故全部排除。
distractors: 其他三项中的文化、自选项目和贬低观点对话中男士均未提及，故全部排除。

items.groupHeader: Questions 9 to 11 are based on the passage you have just heard.
items.stemEn: What does a new study suggest about restaurants including vegetarian sections on their menus?

options.textEn: They may unconsciously help customers choose greener dishes.
They may unintentionally encourage customers to eat meat.
They raise customers' environmental awareness.
They enable customers to eat in a healthy way.

options.text: 它们可能会无意识地帮助顾客选择更环保的菜品。
它们可能会无意中促使顾客吃肉。
它们提高了顾客的环保意识。
它们能让顾客吃得健康。

review.questionTranslation: 关于餐厅在菜单中包含素食部分，一项新研究说明了什么？

evidence.location: 解析册·听力原文 [9] 下划线标注（listening.passages.1）
evidence.quote: Although it sounds counterintuitive, restaurants which include specific vegetarian sections on their menus may be unintentionally encouraging customers to eat meat, a new study suggests.

review.explanation: 文章开头明确提到，尽管这听起来有点违背常理，不过一项新研究表明，那些在菜单中包含专门的素食部分的餐厅，可能会在无意中促使顾客食用肉类。选项B中的 unintentionally encourage customers to eat meat 几乎是文中的原句复现，故B为正确选项。其他三项均与研究结论不符，故全部排除。
distractors: 其他三项均与研究结论不符，故全部排除。

items.groupHeader: Questions 9 to 11 are based on the passage you have just heard.
items.stemEn: How was the study carried out on 750 participants?

options.textEn: By inviting them to taste different kinds of food.
By observing the eating behaviour of strict vegetarians.
By comparing participants eating vegetarian food frequently with those doing so rarely.
By requiring participants to choose a meal as if they were feasting at a family gathering.

options.text: 通过邀请他们品尝不同种类的食物。
通过观察严格素食者的饮食行为。
通过对比经常吃素食的参与者和很少吃素食的参与者。
通过要求参与者在家庭聚餐上吃饭那样选择一份餐食。

review.questionTranslation: 这项研究是如何在750名参与者中开展的？

evidence.location: 解析册·听力原文 [10] 下划线标注（listening.passages.1）
evidence.quote: The study involved 750 people, half of whom frequently ate vegetarian food, and half of whom rarely ate it.

review.explanation: 文章中间部分介绍研究设计时提到，这项研究涉及750人，其中一半人经常吃素食，另一半人很少吃素食。研究人员给了他们不同的菜单，让他们像和朋友外出就餐那样选择一份餐食。选项C是对原文的总结概括，其中的两个频度副词frequently和rarely都是文中出现的，故C为正确选项。

items.groupHeader: Questions 9 to 11 are based on the passage you have just heard.
items.stemEn: How do altered menu designs affect frequent eaters of vegetarian food?

options.textEn: They are less likely to choose a vegetarian dish.
They find vegetarian dishes become more appealing.
They tend to consume larger portions of unhealthy food.
They are less likely to choose dishes recommended by chefs.

options.text: 他们选择素食菜品的可能性更低。
他们觉得素食菜品变得更有吸引力。
他们往往会吃更多分量的不健康食物。
他们选择厨师推荐菜品的可能性更低。

review.questionTranslation: 调整后的菜单设计会对经常吃素食的人产生什么影响？

evidence.location: 解析册·听力原文 [11] 下划线标注（listening.passages.1）
evidence.quote: these altered menu designs backfired with those who ate vegetarian food more frequently, leading them to be less likely to choose a vegetarian dish.

review.explanation: 文章结尾处提到，这些调整后的菜单会让更多很少吃素食的人选择素食，但同样，这些菜单对经常吃素食的人来说却适得其反，会让他们更不太可能选择素食菜品。选项A几乎是原句复现，故A为正确选项。

items.groupHeader: Questions 12 to 15 are based on the passage you have just heard.
items.stemEn: What does the passage say about Nottingham Trent University and the Chinese Academy of Sciences?

options.textEn: They have found a solution to the global problem of air pollution.
They have managed to freeze polluting particles to around -18℃.
They have been seeking a way to prevent pollutants from penetrating indoors.
They have been cooperating closely on developing a new type of air-conditioner.

options.text: 它们找到了全球空气污染问题的解决方案。
它们成功将污染颗粒冷冻到了大约零下18摄氏度。
它们一直在寻找防止污染物进入室内的方法。
它们一直在密切合作研发新型空调。

review.questionTranslation: 关于诺丁汉特伦特大学和中国科学院，文章提到了什么？

evidence.location: 解析册·听力原文 [12] 下划线标注（listening.passages.2）
evidence.quote: Nottingham Trent University and the Chinese Academy of Sciences have been trying to find a way to prevent deadly outdoor air pollution from penetrating indoors.

review.explanation: 文章开头指出，诺丁汉特伦特大学和中国科学院一直在尝试找到防止致命的室外空气污染进入室内的方法。选项C是对这句话的同义转述，为正确答案。选项A在原文中没有提及，选项B是研究过程中发现的“去除污染物的方法”，而非研究成果，选项D中“研发新型空调”并非诺丁汉特伦特大学和中国科学院的核心行动，而是研究成果未来实际运用的方向，故三项均排除。
distractors: 选项A在原文中没有提及，选项B是研究过程中发现的“去除污染物的方法”，而非研究成果，选项D中“研发新型空调”并非诺丁汉特伦特大学和中国科学院的核心行动，而是研究成果未来实际运用的方向，故三项均排除。

items.groupHeader: Questions 12 to 15 are based on the passage you have just heard.
items.stemEn: What do we learn from the passage about existing technologies to purify indoor air?

options.textEn: They can be costly and inefficient.
They are constantly being perfected.
They are by-products of health research.
They can save over 40,000 lives each year.

options.text: 它们可能成本高且效率低。
它们正在不断被完善。
它们是健康研究的副产品。
它们每年可以挽救超过4万人的生命。

review.questionTranslation: 从文章中我们了解到现有室内空气净化技术的什么信息？

evidence.location: 解析册·听力原文 [13] 下划线标注（listening.passages.2）
evidence.quote: While there are some existing technologies to purify indoor air, they can be inefficient, expensive, or produce harmful byproducts.

review.explanation: 文章中间部分指出，虽然目前已有些技术可用于净化室内空气，但这些技术可能效率低、成本高，或者会产生有害的副产品。选项A是对这句话的总结概括，故为正确选项。选项B、C原文未提及，故排除。选项D中“挽救超过4万人的生命”是利用文章中的数据设置的干扰项，与现有室内空气净化技术无关，故也排除。
distractors: 选项B、C原文未提及，故排除。选项D中“挽救超过4万人的生命”是利用文章中的数据设置的干扰项，与现有室内空气净化技术无关，故也排除。

items.groupHeader: Questions 12 to 15 are based on the passage you have just heard.
items.stemEn: What do people tend to do when outdoor air quality is poor?

options.textEn: They keep their windows closed.
They spend a lot more time indoors.
They make more use of air-conditioners.
They try various ways to purify indoor air.

options.text: 他们一直关着窗户。
他们会花更多的时间待在室内。
他们会更多地使用空调。
他们会尝试各种方法净化室内空气。

review.questionTranslation: 当室外空气质量较差时，人们往往会做什么？

evidence.location: 解析册·听力原文 [14] 下划线标注（listening.passages.2）
evidence.quote: When outdoor air quality is poor, people tend to spend even more time indoors

review.explanation: 文章中间部分提到，当室外空气质量较差的时候，人们往往会花更多的时间待在室内。选项B几乎是这句话的原句复现，故为正确选项。其他三项的做法原文均未提及，故全部排除。
distractors: 其他三项的做法原文均未提及，故全部排除。

items.groupHeader: Questions 12 to 15 are based on the passage you have just heard.
items.stemEn: What did Professor Gang Pan of the Chinese Academy of Sciences say about their study?

options.textEn: It shows the importance of eliminating indoor pollution.
It may change the way of future environmental research.
It demonstrates the fruitful cooperation between UK and Chinese scientists.
It may make household appliances serve an additional air cleaner function.

options.text: 它体现了消除室内污染的重要性。
它可能会改变未来环境研究的方式。
它展示了英国和中国科学家之间富有成效的合作。
它可能让家用电器额外具备空气净化器的功能。

review.questionTranslation: 对于他们的研究，中国科学院的潘纲教授是如何评价的？

evidence.location: 解析册·听力原文 [15] 下划线标注（listening.passages.2）
evidence.quote: Our study makes it possible to add an air cleaner option to household appliances in areas which might experience extremely poor air conditions.

review.explanation: 文章最后引用了潘纲教授的话，他明确表示：我们的研究让一件事可能成为现实，那就是在那些空气质量可能极差的地区，给家用电器加上“空气净化器”的选项。选项D是对这句话的同义转述，故为正确选项。

items.groupHeader: Questions 16 to 18 are based on the recording you have just heard.
items.stemEn: What do we learn about the well-known mirror test?

options.textEn: It distinguishes different species of animals.
It reflects distinct traits in animal behaviour.
It demonstrates animals' ability to recognise themselves.
It gauges the level of intelligence of various animal species.

options.text: 它能区分不同的动物物种。
它能反映动物行为中的独特特征。
它能证明动物的自我识别能力。
它能衡量不同动物物种的智力水平。

review.questionTranslation: 关于著名的镜子测试，我们了解到什么？

evidence.location: 解析册·听力原文 [16] 下划线标注（listening.lectures.1）
evidence.quote: A certain species of fish recently passed the well-known mirror test—this is a test that demonstrates self-recognition in the animals.

review.explanation: 在讲话开头，讲话者便提到，某种鱼类近日通过了著名的“镜子测试”——这是一种用于证明动物具备自我识别能力的测试。由此得出，正确答案为C。

items.groupHeader: Questions 16 to 18 are based on the recording you have just heard.
items.stemEn: What does the study by the speaker's team show about the fish they experimented with?

options.textEn: It meets few of the behavioural criteria set in the mirror test.
It behaves similarly to animals capable of self-recognition.
It removes marks from itself to show self-awareness.
It matches children over 18 months in intelligence.

options.text: 它几乎不符合镜子测试所设定的行为标准。
它的行为与具备自我识别能力的动物相似。
它清除自身标记以展现自我意识。
它的智力与18个月以上的人类幼儿相当。

review.questionTranslation: 讲话者团队的研究显示，他们实验所用的鱼类有何表现？

evidence.location: 解析册·听力原文 [17] 下划线标注（listening.lectures.1）
evidence.quote: What is less clear is whether these behaviours should be considered as evidence that fish are self-aware

banked_cloze.fullTextTranslation:
我们人类总爱相信自己独特的，但科学技术却一再证明这种信念是错误的。人们[26]曾以为只有人类才会使用工具，组建团队或传承文化，但科学已经表明其他动物也能做到这些事情。
与此同时，技术已逐一否定了那些宣称[27]认知任务必须依赖人类大脑的说法。第一台加法机发明于1623年。而就在去年，一件计算机生成的作品赢得了艺术比赛。我相信计算机达到并[28]超越人类智能的时刻即将到来。
当机器的智慧与创造力超越最聪明的人类时，人类的智慧与创造力将如何被看待呢？很可能会呈现为一种分层次的状态。在某些[29]领域，即使计算机做得更好，人们依然看重人类亲力亲为。自从一台计算机击败世界冠军加里·卡斯帕罗夫以来，已经过去了二十五年，但人类国际象棋并未消失。
在其他领域，人类技能将显得昂贵且[30]多余。以插画为例：大多数读者并不在意杂志文章[31]配图出自人类之手还是计算机之作——他们只要求图片贴切、新颖，或许还要[32]有趣。
当然，这并不是非黑即白的简单问题。许多领域将呈现[33]混合形态：少数人类能找到幸运的立足点，但大部分工作由计算机完成，就像当今的制造业，大量工作由机器人承担，但仍需人类[34]监督机器运作。
若以历史为鉴，几乎可以肯定的是：人工智能的进步将导致更多岗位[35]消失；掌握人类独有技能的创意工作者会变得更加富有，但人数将会减少，而拥有创意技术的人将成为新的超级富豪。

information_matching.fullTextTranslation:
A) 项目、人际关系和工作未必总能按计划顺利进行——而且往往不清楚何时该放弃。我们常听人说“半途而废者永无胜算”，但有时候，止损是最明智的决定。
B) 想想那段明明已走到尽头你却依然紧抓不放的感情，或是那份尽管老板让你痛苦不堪你却仍在坚守的工作。我们很多人都会试图抓住最后一丝希望，觉得自己能让情况好转——无论是什么“情况”。虽然坚持不懈通常是一种极好的品质，但它也可能让你在早已不值得的事情上过度投入。
C) 作为一名高管教练，我和许多富有热情、勤奋肯干的领导者合作，他们都不愿“半途而废”。[43]但最睿智的领导者懂得区分“过早放弃”与“执着于不该执着之事”的不同。
D) 我们都容易陷入“沉没成本谬误”——这是一种无意识的偏见，会让我们在已经投入了时间、精力或金钱的事情上固执坚持，即便放弃它会带来更大的益处。我们深知无法收回已经付出的资源，于是便选择坚持下去：在本该叫停的项目上继续投入，继续留在本该结束的关系中，或是因为已经读了一半，就坚持读完一本早已不喜欢、本该放下的书。如果你向来“不愿放弃”，那么你可能尤其容易受这种偏见影响。
E) “沉没成本谬误”让我们过度担忧“继续前行会失去的东西”，却对“不继续前行所要付出的代价”考虑不足。[39]要抵消这种偏见，你需要刻意将注意力重新聚焦于“收益”，这样才能更客观地权衡各种选择。不妨问问自己：现在止损，我可能会获得什么？你会变得更快乐，还是能腾出时间把握另一个（更好的）机会？接着再问问自己：硬撑下去，我要付出什么代价？比如，你是否可能在已经损失的基础上，再投更多钱进去？又或者，是否会因此耗尽精力而错失其他更有前景的可能？
F) 控制错觉也会干扰我们做出最佳判断，导致我们高估自己掌控事态、获得积极结果的能力。这种偏见赋予我们一种掌控感，还能促进心理健康。但它同样可能让我们在一条注定失败的道路上越走越远。尤其当这种偏见与“我从不言弃”的心态结合时，[36]感觉自己对某件事或某个人拥有超出实际的掌控力会让我们面临更大的风险，在本该抽身的时候反而加大投入。
G) 要抵消这种偏见，你可以审视自身情况，制作一份简单的两栏清单，分别列出“可控之事”与“不可控之事”。务必深思熟虑。你或许能够影响别人和各种局势，但你无法强迫他们改变，也不能强求事情按你的意愿发展。
H) [45]明确自己能掌控什么、不能掌控什么，对于做出是否放弃还是继续坚持的明智决定至关重要。手中有了这份书面清单，你就能确保自己把注意力集中在可控之事上，也能更理智地评估继续投入是否值得。把精力和情感耗费在不可控的事情上，只会让人身心俱疲、倍感无力。
I) [41]研究表明，人们会将自我认同与社会地位同自身所投入的事务绑定在一起。而正因为我们认同自己投入的事务，从中抽身时，才会让人感觉自我认同或社会地位受到了威胁。
J) [38]以我的客户瑞安为例，她是一家科技公司的管理者。瑞安已在一个设计项目上投入了两年时间和大量精力，但该项目始终未能达到预期成果。然而，想到自己付出了这么多却要放弃，她感到难以接受。当我和瑞安一同探讨，她究竟该终止还是该继续坚持这个由她牵头的项目时，她表示：“关键是，我从不言弃。”这种单一固化的自我认知正在混淆她的判断，限制她的行动选择。
K) 我们的自我认知与身份认同是能够影响自身行为的心理概念。[37]如果你强烈认定自己不是一个会半途而废的人，反而可能会因为这种狭隘僵化的自我认知陷入某种行动模式中无法自拔。要克服这种内在的阻碍，不妨回想一下自己拥有的其他积极特质与性格优势。你可以问问自己：我还具备（或渴望具备）哪些额外优势能帮我应对当下的处境？比如，当我问瑞安，在做决策时她需要发挥自己性格里的哪些其他积极特质，她回答道：“洞察力与勇气。”
L) 现在，试着从自身这些特质的视角来审视你的处境。你个性中敏锐洞察的那一面会给出什么建议？勇敢无畏的那一面呢？从这些不同特质的角度考虑你的决策，会让你意识到自己其实拥有更多选择。同时，主动寻求外部的信息来源也很有帮助，而不是仅仅依赖自身的想法和直觉。但重要的是，你要明确征求的是哪些人的意见。
M) [40]理想情况下，要去找那些对你的决策投入度没那么高的人。比如，如果你正在考虑是否要关停自己的创业项目，那就去联系其他创业者，而非只和你的合伙人商议。同理，如果你想寻求感情方面的建议，应该去咨询那些没有卷入你感情波折的人，而不是只依赖自己的挚友。无论哪种情况，我都建议你先说明自己的处境，再接着问这样一个问题：“你会如何处理这种情况？”
N) [44]或者，你也可以去找硬性数据，这些数据可以揭示你正考虑的任何一项事业的实际成功概率。沿用创业项目的例子：数据就是你最可靠的帮手。借助数据，你可以跳出对创业构想的主观偏爱，转而考虑资金消耗率与增长计划、行业增长率，以及其他能预判初创企业成败的因素。外部信息来源能帮你看到一些你原本可能忽略的视角和可能性。
O) 当某个起初看似前景大好的事物，最终并未如我们设想的那般发展时，我们可能会过度自责。[42]没有人愿意承认自己做了错误的决定，尤其是当做出明智决策是你极为看重的特质时。应对这种情况最有效的策略就是，让自己休息一下。自我同情不仅能增强你的韧性，提升你的情商，培养你对他人的同理心，还能助力你优化表现，培养出成长型思维模式。
P) 与其反复纠结、苛责自己，不如转而关注你能从当下的处境中学到的经验。比如瑞安就意识到，自己在主导这个设计项目的过程中锻炼出了多项新技能，也培养了领导能力。尽管最终决定放弃这个项目，但她依然为自己敢于尝试而感到欣慰，也对这段经历所带来的收获心怀感激。
Q) 不可否认，坚持能使我们走向成功。但为了你的身心健康，学会区分“过早放弃”与“执着于注定失败的道路”至关重要。放手或许很难，但这么做会释放你的时间、精力与心力，让你得以畅想新的可能，追逐新的机遇。

careful_reading::passage_one.fullTextTranslation:
[46]作为相互依存的个体，我们无法脱离他人而蓬勃发展。我们喜欢与志同道合、有共同兴趣，或同样坚信我们所重视之事的人共事。这一点在我们将自己组织成各种集合体的方式中很明显，比如国家、地区、社区、组织和家庭。
你所在的群体是否拥有强烈的集体意识或共同信仰？群体成员之间是否存在相互依存的关系？你是否认为这个群体是你生活中重要的一部分？如果你的答案都是肯定的，那么你正体验着一种微观层面的团结。
何为团结？词典中最简明的定义是：“一群人之间统一的观点、情感、目标或利益。”
[47]在我们所处的这个日益多元化的社会中，团结呈现出复杂而多面的特征。它在独特的个体之间建立了相互依存的纽带。这些个体生活在快速变化的环境中，并且在复杂的分工体系下工作。
团结的一个层面与社群主义的原则十分契合。[48]在这种情境下，个体放弃自身利益以服务公共利益。然而，社群主义对社会凝聚力和排他性的严格遵循，限制了个体差异与偏好的表达和实践。因此，为了维护群体的统一性，个性与自主性便被牺牲了。
[49]团结也被视为对极端个人主义和选择自由的一种反对。它反对不受限制的个人所持的自由主义理念，这些人将社会视为阻碍他们自由选择和按照自身利益行事的绊脚石，完全不考虑自身行为会对他人造成何种影响。
[50]尽管团结具有多面性，但社会理论家们仍将其视为推动社会秩序与进步的关键因素。他们认为，随着人类社会日益多元化，要想存续，就需要基于差异建立更多新的纽带。鉴于此，他们认为真正的团结不仅仅是基于共同利益的肤浅关系。团结不仅仅是人们战略性盘算其能为自身带来多少利益的产物。它也不是一个基于“你我联手对抗全世界”原则的排他性小团体。相反，它是包容的，且并非强迫的。出于团结而行动，意味着相互支持、彼此声援——承认一个人的命运与另一个人的命运息息相关。这种纽带以合作实践为特征，并通过关怀他人福祉或共同利益而得到强化。它为捍卫人类尊严而战，倾听并回应最弱势群体的呼声。

careful_reading::passage_two.fullTextTranslation:
有些人总是反复给出别人并不想听的建议，这或许是出于好意，真心想提供帮助。而另一些人这么做，则可能是出于一种通过影响他人来获得自我价值感的心态。[51]一项研究发现，相比于权力欲较弱的人，权力欲较强的人更爱主动给出建议。
[51]这些人往往打着无私的幌子把建议强加给你，背后的驱动力其实是想借此获得掌控感，彰显自身权力。不过，他们自己可能并没有完全意识到这一点。
[52]这类人还可能表现出过度的情绪脆弱问题：他们很容易心烦意乱，并且需要很长时间才能平息情绪。这或许是因为他们在童年时期，只有通过大哭大闹的方式，才能让自己的情绪得到关注和认可，这种成长经历让他们养成了习惯，在大多数情况下，遇到不顺心的事，都会做出过激反应。
当有人为了让自己感到更有权力而向你提建议时，其背后往往隐藏着焦虑情绪，而这也通常会被听建议的人察觉到。[53]这种情况下，你很容易忍不住对这个提出建议的人做出强硬的回应，指责对方在操控你，但这种做法可能会适得其反。
[54]如果提建议这件事是支撑某人自我价值感的重要来源，那么直截了当地拒绝就会被他们视作一种威胁。这会触发他们的“战斗或逃跑反应”，可能会让他们变本加厉地寻求自我认可，甚至引发更大的冲突。
关键的应对原则是认可对方的心意，但不必过度认同其观点。你可以让对方知道，你已经听取了他们的建议，也理解他们的出发点，同时也不必接受“没有他们的帮助你就无法解决问题”这种可能产生负面影响的说法。最好这样说：“谢谢你的提议。我已经有了自己的处理方案，但很感谢你提供的角度，我会考虑的。以后需要帮忙的话，我再跟你说，可以吗？”
如果你不擅长巧妙地设立边界，那就优先锻炼自己的情绪调节能力。尽管频繁收到别人自作主张的建议会让你感到不适，但如果能以同情的态度回应，局面可能会更快平息。
尽管那些自作主张的提议通常并非提议者有意为之，但很多听建议的人总会因为这些自作主张的意见而感到压力，被冒犯，或者只是心生厌烦。如果觉得有必要，针对这种情况设立边界是完全合理的做法，这能让你获得更强的情绪安全感。
[55]设立边界时，最好考虑到对方之所以这么做的深层原因。这样可以避免不必要的冲突，减少更多的压力。

passage.title: Do You Know When to Quit Wisely?

paragraphs.text: Projects, relationships, and jobs don't always work out as planned—and it's not always clear when to give up. We've all repeatedly heard the saying that "quitters never win," but sometimes the best decision is to cut our losses.

Think about that relationship you held on to even after it had run its course or the job you stayed in despite your boss making you miserable. Many of us try to hold onto the last ray of hope, thinking we can make it work, whatever "it" is. And while perseverance is generally an excellent quality, it may also incline you to over-invest in something that is no longer a good idea.

As an executive coach, I work with numerous passionate and hard-working leaders who don't want to "quit." But the smartest leaders learn to discern the difference between quitting too soon and holding onto something that they shouldn't.

We are all susceptible to the sunk-cost delusion, an unconscious bias that leads us to persist in an endeavor we have already invested time, effort, or money into—even when abandoning it would be more beneficial. We realize that we can't get back the resources we've given, so we persevere—investing in a project that should be halted, staying in a relationship that should be over, or finishing a book we no longer enjoy and should put down, because we're already halfway through it. If quitting is "not your thing", you may be especially susceptible to this bias.

The sunk-cost delusion causes us to overly worry about what we'll lose if we move on and not think enough about the costs of not moving on. To offset this bias, deliberately refocus your thinking on the gains so you can more objectively weigh the alternatives. Ask yourself: What might I gain by cutting my losses now? Will you be happier or have time for another (better) opportunity? Then ask yourself: What will it cost me to soldier on? For example, is it possible that you'll be throwing more good money after what you've already lost? Or that you won't have the energy to capitalize on other promising possibilities?

The illusion of control can also interfere with our best judgment, leading us to overestimate our ability to control events and attain a positive outcome. This bias gives us a sense of agency and can promote mental health. However, the bias can also result in escalating commitment to a losing course of action. Especially when combined with an "I'm not a quitter" mentality, feeling like we have more control over an event or person than we do puts us at risk of doubling down when we should pull out.

To counteract this bias, consider your situation and make a simple two-column list of what's in your control and what's not. Think rigorously. While you may be able to influence other people and various circumstances, you can't force them to change or go your way.

Getting clear on what you can control and what you can't is essential to making a quality decision about whether to call it quits or persevere. With a written list in hand, you can ensure you focus on what you can control and better assess whether your continued efforts are worth the expense. Expending effort and emotion on things you can't control can be both draining and disempowering.

Research indicates that people link their self-identity and social status to their commitments. And because we identify with our commitments, withdrawing from one can feel like a threat to our identity or status.

Take my client Ryan, a leader at a technology company. Ryan had invested two years and a lot of effort in a design project that wasn't delivering the needed outcomes, but the thought of abandoning it after all she had put in was hard to bear. As Ryan and I explored whether she should cancel the initiative she'd been leading or continue to persevere, she stated, "The thing is, I'm not a quitter." This singular, fixed sense of self was clouding her judgment and limiting her choices for action.

Our self-concept and identity are mental concepts that influence our behavior. If you strongly identify as not being a quitter, you can end up staying stuck in a course of action due to your narrow and rigid self-concept. To overcome this kind of internal obstacle, recall your other positive traits and personality characteristics. Ask yourself: What additional strengths do I have (or aspire to have) that would be helpful to employ here? For example, when I asked Ryan what other positive qualities from her personality she needed to leverage for decision making, she replied, "Discernment and bravery."

Now, examine your situation through the lens of each of these facets of yourself. What does the discerning part of you say? The brave part? Considering your decision through these different characteristics will enable you to see that you have more choices. It's also helpful to seek external sources of information, rather than relying solely on your thinking and instincts. But it's important to think through whose opinions you solicit.

Ideally, seek out people who are less invested in your decision than you are. If you're considering whether to shut down your entrepreneurial venture, for instance, reach out to other founders as opposed to just your business partner. Similarly, if you're looking for love advice, ask someone removed from the ups and downs of your relationship instead of relying only on your best friend. In all cases, I recommend describing your situation and following up with a question like: "How would you manage this situation?"

Alternately, you could also seek out hard data that illuminates your real chance of success in whatever endeavor you are contemplating. Sticking with the example of the entrepreneurial venture, numbers are your best friend. Use them to remove yourself from the love you have for this idea and consider your burn rate relative to growth plan, industry growth rates, and other factors that predict start-up success. External sources of information can help you see angles and possibilities you might not have considered.

When something that seemed so promising at the start doesn't turn out the way we imagined, we can become overly self-critical. Nobody likes to feel that they've made a poor decision, especially if making intelligent decisions is a quality you hold in high esteem. The most effective strategy here is to give yourself a break. Practicing self-compassion increases your resilience (韧性), emotional intelligence, compassion toward others, and can boost your performance as well as help you develop a growth mindset.

Instead of deliberating and criticizing yourself, focus instead on what you can learn from this situation. For example, Ryan recognized she had developed various new skills and leadership capabilities from leading the design project. And despite ultimately deciding to drop it, she was still happy she had tried and grateful for what the experience taught her.

Undeniably, perseverance can help us succeed. But for your wellbeing, it's important to learn how to distinguish quitting too soon and clinging to a losing course of action. While letting go can be difficult, it will free up your time, energy, and mental space to imagine new possibilities and pursue new opportunities.

blocks.text: As interdependent beings we cannot thrive independent of others. We like to work with people who are like-minded, with whom we share a common interest, or who also believe in a cause we are serious about. This is evident in how we have organised ourselves into various collective groups such as nations, regions, communities, organisations, and families.

Does the group you belong to have a strong collective consciousness or shared beliefs? Is there interdependence among its members? Do you consider this group a significant part of your existence? If your answers are affirmative, then you are experiencing a micro version of solidarity.
What is solidarity? Its simplest definition in the dictionary is: "...a unifying opinion, feeling, purpose or interest among a group of people."

In this increasingly diverse society we live in, solidarity takes on a complex and multifaceted character as it forms bonds of interdependence among unique individuals living in a fast-changing environment and working within a complex division of labour.

One facet of solidarity fits well with the principles of communitarianism (社群主义). In this setting, individuals give up their own interests to serve the common good. However, its strict adherence to social cohesiveness and exclusiveness restricts expression and practice of individual differences and preferences. Consequently, individuality and autonomy is sacrificed to maintain the unity of the group.

Solidarity is also viewed as a reaction to the extreme emphasis on individualism and freedom of choice. It goes against the liberal idea of unrestricted individuals who see society as a hindrance to their freedom to make choices and to act according to what is good for them regardless of how these will affect others.

But despite its many facets, social theorists have viewed solidarity as a key factor in bringing about order and progress in society. They believe that for human society to survive as it becomes more diverse, more new bonds need to be formed based on the differences. In the light of this, they regard a genuine solidarity as more than just shallow relationships based on common interests. Solidarity is not just a product of strategic calculations of how much it will benefit the self. It is not an exclusive class founded on the you-and-me-against-the-world principle. Rather, it is inclusive and is not forced. Acting out of solidarity means supporting and standing up for each other—in recognition that one's fate is in the fate of the other. It is a bond characterised by cooperative practices and strengthened by the concern for the well-being of others or the common good. It fights for the protection of human dignity and listens to and acts on the cries of the most vulnerable.

blocks.text: People who repeatedly give unwanted advice can be well-meaning and genuinely want to help. Others might do this out of a sense of self-worth around the ability to influence others. One study found that people with a high tendency to seek power were more likely to give advice than those with an opposite tendency.
Under the guise (外表) of unselfishness, people may be driven to give you unwanted advice because it makes them feel powerful or in control. They may not be fully aware of this drive, however.

These people may also display a problematic degree of emotional vulnerability, becoming upset very quickly, and taking a long time to calm down. It is possible that their emotions were only validated in childhood when they were at their loudest, encouraging them to adopt responses to discomfort that are excessive in most situations.

When someone is giving advice in order to make themselves feel more powerful, there is underlying anxiety to their behavior that recipients of the advice tend to notice. It can be tempting in this situation to react harshly to the advice giver and to accuse them of being manipulative, but this approach might produce an undesirable result.

If the act of giving advice is contributing actively to someone's feelings of self-worth, an outright (直率的) rejection may be perceived as a threat, activating their fight-or-flight response, possibly causing them to double down on their validation-seeking behavior, or leading to a larger conflict.

The key is to validate without over-identifying. You can let them know that you have heard them and appreciate where they are coming from without taking on the potentially damaging narrative that you could not have gotten by without their help. You had better say something like, "Thanks for the idea. I have my own plan for handling this, but I really appreciate your perspective and will take it into consideration. Can I let you know when I need help in the future?"

If you have trouble setting boundaries tactfully, prioritize working on your own ability to self-regulate. As uncomfortable as it may make you continuously receiving unwanted advice, if you can respond with compassion, the situation will likely diffuse much faster.

Though it is usually not the intended outcome of giving unsolicited advice, many who receive it often feel stressed, offended, or simply annoyed by unwanted suggestions. Setting a boundary in this regard, if you feel you need one, is perfectly reasonable and something that can bring you increased emotional safety.
It is best to set boundaries in a way that takes into account the individual's underlying reasons for doing what they are doing to avoid unnecessary conflict and more stress.

evidence.location: 解析引用（原书对照短语·第一段最后一句（原书作one study，原文句首大写））

review.explanation: 【定位】根据题干信息词one study可以把答案线索初步定位至第一段最后一句。【解析】第一段最后一句提到：“一项研究发现，相比于权力欲较弱的人，权力欲较强的人更爱主动给出建议。”第二段第一句接着对此进行了进一步阐释：“这些人……背后的驱动力其实是想借此获得掌控感，彰显自身权力。”选项D与此表述一致，故为正确答案。选项A和选项B都是文章开头提到的“有些人”的动机，但不是该研究的具体发现；选项C是权力寻求倾向可能带来的结果或自我感觉，并非研究发现本身，故这三项均排除。
distractors: 选项A和选项B都是文章开头提到的“有些人”的动机，但不是该研究的具体发现；选项C是权力寻求倾向可能带来的结果或自我感觉，并非研究发现本身，故这三项均排除。

review.explanation: 【定位】根据题干信息词react to the rejection可以把答案线索定位至第五段。【解析】第五段明确指出：“……那么直截了当地拒绝就会被他们视作一种威胁。这会触发他们的‘战斗或逃跑反应’，可能会让他们变本加厉地寻求自我认可，甚至引发更大的冲突。”因此，提议者直接的反应是把这样的拒绝视作威胁，故选项A为正确答案。选项B与文中“double down on”（变本加厉）相悖；选项C是提议者有了将拒绝视作威胁的反应后可能导致的后果之一，所以“做好准备”不是必然的直接心理反应，“视作威胁”才是；选项D在文中未提及，故这三项均排除。

evidence.quote: avoid unnecessary conflict

parts.prompt: Directions: For this part, you are allowed 30 minutes to write an essay that begins with the sentence "While striving for the Chinese Dream, young people enjoy more opportunities to realize their self-worth." You can make comments, cite examples or use your personal experiences to develop your essay. You should write at least 150 words but no more than 200 words. You should copy the sentence given in quotes at the beginning of your essay.

reference.modelEssay:
While striving for the Chinese Dream, young people enjoy more opportunities to realize their self-worth. This national aspiration not only maps out the country's development path but also provides diverse platforms for young people to apply their talents, bridging the gap between personal ambition and national progress.
The opportunities are evident in several key areas. First, in technological innovation, the state's support for the renewable energy sector has enabled many young people to engage in the research and development of new energy vehicles. This not only helps China take the lead globally in this field, but also allows these young people to gain industry recognition and a strong sense of accomplishment. Second, on the cultural front, there is more encouragement for diverse talents in arts, new media, and digital content creation. Young content creators use short videos to introduce traditional Chinese crafts like paper-cutting and porcelain-making to global audiences, helping spread Chinese culture while establishing their own influence as cultural ambassadors.
In short, the Chinese Dream provides young people with a stage to turn aspirations into reality. Through opportunities in national key sectors, the realization of personal self-worth goes hand in hand with driving the country's progress.
reference.commentary:
1 以给定句子引出话题，描述“中国梦”和“年轻人的机遇”之间的内在联系，为下文论述做铺垫。
2 针对机遇的具体体现，给出了不同方面的具体例子，分别用First、Second引出。
3 总结全文，升华主题。
reference.shenTi: 题目要求考生写一篇以“在为实现中国梦而奋斗的过程中，年轻人有了更多实现自我价值的机遇。”为开头的作文，考生可以通过发表评论、举例子或描述个人经历展开论述。根据题目提示，作文可以采取以下布局：开头段以给定句子引出话题，简要阐释两者的内在联系；中间段具体举例说明，展示年轻人如何把握机遇以实现自我价值；结尾段总结全文，升华主题。
reference.essayTranslation:
在为实现中国梦而奋斗的过程中，年轻人有了更多实现自我价值的机遇。这一民族愿景不仅规划了国家的发展路径，而且为年轻人提供了施展才华的多种平台，搭建起个人抱负与国家进步之间的桥梁。
这些机遇在几个关键领域显而易见。首先，在科技创新领域，国家对新能源产业的支持让许多年轻人得以投身于新能源汽车的研发工作。这不仅有助于中国在这个领域引领全球，也让这些年轻人获得了行业认可和强烈的成就感。其次，在文化层面，对艺术、新媒体和数字内容创作等领域的多元化人才给予了更多鼓励。年轻的内容创作者通过短视频向全球观众介绍剪纸、瓷器制作等中国传统工艺，在助力中华文化传播的同时，建立自身作为文化大使的影响力。
总之，中国梦为年轻人提供了将理想变为现实的舞台。借助国家重点领域的发展机遇，个人自我价值的实现与推动国家发展进步相辅相成。

parts.sourceZh: 中华民族崇尚自强自立的精神，这一精神深植于中国文化之中，是民族生存与发展的重要支撑。改革开放以来，中国在自强自立的征程上，持续加大科研投入，在信息技术、人工智能、航天工程等领域不断取得新突破。5G网络覆盖全国，远程医疗发展迅速，电子支付的使用全球领先，嫦娥探月工程展现了航天领域引人注目的发展。自强自立精神成为推动国家现代化进程的强大动力，激励着中国人民为实现民族复兴(rejuvenation)的中国梦不断奋进。

reference.referenceEn: The Chinese nation upholds the spirit of self-improvement and self-reliance, which is deeply rooted in Chinese culture and serves as a vital pillar for the nation's survival and development. Since the reform and opening-up, China has continuously increased investment in scientific research in its journey of self-improvement and self-reliance, achieving new breakthroughs in fields such as information technology, artificial intelligence, and aerospace engineering. 5G networks now cover the entire country; telemedicine has developed rapidly; the adoption of electronic payment leads the world, and Chang'e lunar exploration program has demonstrated remarkable progress in aerospace. The spirit of self-improvement and self-reliance has become a powerful driving force in advancing the nation's modernization, inspiring the Chinese people to strive relentlessly toward realizing the Chinese Dream of national rejuvenation.
reference.commentary:
1. 第一句：本句为阐述核心精神的定义句。主句“中华民族崇尚……精神”译为The Chinese nation upholds the spirit of...。后两个分句“这一精神深植于……”和“是……重要支撑”共同说明该精神的特点与作用，故合并译为由which引导的非限制性定语从句，并使用and连接两个并列谓语is deeply rooted和serves as，使句子逻辑紧凑、修饰关系清晰。
2. 第二句：本句描述具体实践与成就。时间状语“改革开放以来”译为Since the reform and opening-up。“在……征程上”译为介词短语in its journey of...作状语。两个主要动作“加大投入”和“取得突破”具有先后与因果关系，将前者作为主句谓语和宾语has increased investment，后者则译为现在分词短语achieving breakthroughs...作结果状语。
3. 第三句：本句为并列结构，列举四项具体成就，采用四个独立分句，用分号和and连接，形成清晰的排比列举效果。时态上，“5G网络”和“电子支付”描述当前普遍状态，使用一般现在时；“远程医疗”和“嫦娥探月工程”强调已完成并持续产生影响，使用现在完成时。“嫦娥探月工程”译为Chang'e lunar exploration program。
4. 第四句：本句总结“精神”的作用与影响。句子主干“精神成为强大动力”译为The spirit...has become a powerful driving force。“推动……”作为“动力”的具体指向，译为介词短语in advancing。“激励着……”是精神成为动力后产生的伴随性结果，译为现在分词短语inspiring...作状语。“为实现……不断奋进”译为不定式短语to strive...toward realizing...作目的状语。“民族复兴”译为national rejuvenation。
